data.title: task list --search matches words with the search engine; the TUI / filter stays a substring
data.why: One product had two ideas of what matches means: kadence search (tokenized BM25 with a coverage gate) and task list --search (lowercase substring over title, description and comments). The substring was blind to acceptance criteria and is the one agents do not get told about, so a task list --search and a search --kind task could disagree about the same journal. Now both use one tokenizer and one coverage rule; task list keeps its flag, fields and filters, returns every matching task rather than the top five, and ranks by relevance unless --sort is given. The TUI filter is different in kind: it narrows the board as a person types, where 'coo' must already show 'cookie', and no agent uses it.
data.rejected: Keep the substring and point at search when it comes back empty: two matchers stay in the product and drift; Retire task list --search in favour of search --kind task: breaks every script that passes the flag, and loses the combination with --status, --overdue and --sort; Put the TUI filter on the engine too: word matching cannot filter on a prefix while someone is still typing
